title: The Black Hole
abstract: The Black Hole turns a malfunctioning photocopier into a portable opening through solid surfaces. This analysis examines how the film teaches its visual rule, then converts curiosity into opportunism, theft, and entrapment.
image_captions: An exhausted office worker establishes the film’s blue-gray baseline
The impossible black circle first appears as a physical object on paper
The photocopier frames discovery as an ordinary workplace interruption
The film’s central visual rule becomes clear through tactile experimentation
Small temptation escalates into deliberate theft at the vending machine
The final safe image turns shortcut-seeking into entrapment
